mechanism.summary: Zero new server endpoints. All checklist signals read from existing READ endpoints.
mechanism.step_1_create_application: GET /api/applications — reuses the screen's OWN already-fetched `apps` state (the same counter the 'Конструктор' tile already shows); not a second fetch. done = apps > 0.
mechanism.step_2_connect_llm_key: GET /api/agents + the pre-existing exported pure function resolveAssistantBinding(agents) from screen-llm-connections.jsx:176-184 (imported, not duplicated). Finds agent_type==='assistant', done = assistantConnectionId != null. Chosen over GET /api/llm-connections because that endpoint requires the llm_connection:configure capability (403s a non-admin tenant member); GET /api/agents is gated only by withAuth, so the step honestly resolves for any authenticated user.
mechanism.step_3_ask_assistant: GET /api/assistant/threads — done when threads.some(t => t.message_count > 0). Same list/shape the assistant screen itself renders.
mechanism.step_4_optional_configure_rights: GET /api/rights/tenant-state — rendered ONLY when can_manage===true resolved successfully; otherwise structurally absent from the list (mirrors the T-0572 ADR principle applied to write-forms: can_manage:false ⇒ absent, not disabled/unchecked). Excluded from the hide-criterion for the same reason.
mechanism.degradation: Each of the 3 mandatory signals is wrapped exactly like the screen's existing fetchCount() helper: any network/HTTP/parse failure resolves to null, never throws — the step stays visible without a checkmark and its CTA link remains clickable. The whole strip auto-hides (returns null) ONLY when all three mandatory signals are CONFIRMED true — a null/false/loading state keeps the strip visible, which is the safe default.
mechanism.inbox_empty_state: screen-inbox.jsx's EmptyState branch now inspects (tab, exec, counts.all) already held in component state — no new fetch. tab==='all' && !exec && counts.all===0 renders an action CTA (navigate('/processes'), route pre-existing in shell.jsx); every other combination renders a distinct 'empty in this view' message without the action, to avoid implying /processes would fix a filter-scoped empty view.
